title: The mystery volcano that buried a kingdom 🌋
subject: volcano
description:
Do you think Pamatan will ever be found? 👇

For decades, ice cores from Greenland and Antarctica showed a giant eruption around 1257, but no one knew where it was. In 2013, scientists traced it to Samalas on Lombok, Indonesia, a blast that buried the capital Pamatan and was followed by famine in Europe.

Sources: Lavigne et al., PNAS (2013); NPR, "Scientists May Have Source For 1257 A.D. Mystery Eruption" (2013); Live Science / Inside Science, "Source of 13th Century Volcanic Calamity Discovered" (2013); Discover, "Samalas in Indonesia Identified as Source of the 1257 A.D. 'Missing' Eruption" (Erik Klemetti, 2013); Durham University, "The sun was dark..." (Dr Alex Brown, 2026); Londonist, "That Time A Volcano Killed A Third Of Londoners".

scenes.text: A royal capital still lies buried under this island.
Ice cores from both poles held a huge sulfur spike from 1257, from a volcano no one could find.
In 2013, Franck Lavigne's team traced it to Samalas, on Lombok in Indonesia: 8 times Krakatoa's sulfur.
Palm-leaf chronicles say the capital, Pamatan, was buried in ash. It's never been found.
In England, monk Matthew Paris wrote that 15,000 of London's poor starved.
Samalas itself is gone. Where it stood, there's a crater lake.
